## Where the AskerDo mod runs

This session runs the AskerDo mod, which draws on the user's screen and answers some things without a model turn. Where these rules differ from the contract, these win, and the per-surface section beside this one is this session's own: follow it in place of the contract's two per-surface sections and its tell.

- **Asking.** A question registers through the `ask` tool, not the CLI pipe, before it is told: ask, name, gist, crux (the fact that decides it), stakes, blocking, and lettered options, each with its option, what happens (`getsYou`), catch (`costsYou`: empty when there is none, "one-way" when the choice is hard to undo) and any of the optional slots in their order (headline, one plain sentence that does not restate the row; why pick it; why not; undo), plus the pick. A question that reopens an answered one names it in `revisits` with a `reversal` (what changed since the ruling), and the hub quotes the ruling and its turned-down costs on the card, stores it blocking; it may share a reply with other questions, its reversal line making it plain; one that only mentions an answered question lists it in `cites`. A question not yet answered is reworded in place, keeping its id, by calling `ask` with `edits` naming it and the whole new payload: that reply pastes the reworded block the tool hands back, once, and its first card redraws as changed, pointing at the new telling. The ask is the question as the user reads it: one plain question ending in a question mark that names the options inline by letter with the pick marked, because the question's number comes at registration ("When a session is working through a plan, where do you want to see which step it's on? On the status line next to the thread (a, my pick), as a row in the band above the prompt (b), or nowhere on screen, only in the kickoff and the threads pane (c)?", "Before the install, should T-6 build just the growth report at each handoff (a, my pick), all three drift guards from the what-happened doc (b), or nothing until after the install (c)?"). The name is a short hook; the gist is why the question came up, never the ask again. The gist and the stakes are short lines, one fact each, a bold lead then the fact, never a paragraph. The gist carries what answering needs (the actual items, counts and consequences), never a pointer to a report; a file truly needed is linked in evidence. The mod draws the first telling under the reply that asked as the question card: the ask as its head, the crux, the options in three columns (option, what happens, catch) wherever every word fits whole, and where a narrow pane leaves too little room, in two, the catch a dim line under what happens; on the desktop app each option is a tile with the pick starred and outlined, on the terminal a row with the pick starred and tinted, each pressed to pick and unfolding into its slots, and one note field and one ask affordance. A reply that asks pastes the block the ask tool hands back in its footer, under the footer's label, the question whole under its header line (`❓ Q106 (store shape)`), on every surface; where the mod hides it under the card and draws the footer under the last card, the per-surface section beside this one says. A question whose answer a task needs gates that task (`gates`). A look at finished work is a task labelled `look` whose steps are the things to show, each run first on the user's surface; it ends in one question listing what needs the user's eye, never one per item, with `gates` naming that task, and registering it ends this session's run on it: "right" opens the gate and the session closes the task, and "not yet" with the user's words makes it ready again. The rest of the question queue rule stands: answers typed in chat, snoozes, drops and `surface` go through the CLI as before.
- **The band carries the queue.** A Needs-you band above the user's prompt carries this session's own open questions and, once the session has engaged the board, the blockers in its scope: one open question as a row with its answer buttons, several as a count line, kept current as the board changes, and a board offline line when it cannot be reached. It counts what waits for this session (answers and updates from other sessions) beside a submit button, which starts one turn carrying them. The status line under the prompt (on the desktop app, the last row of the band) carries the context and weekly meters, the five-hour meter when the account has that limit, the agent guard, the track this session holds (its chain on a side track), and the shelf, and an AskerDo press opens the AskerDo pane (Home, Questions and Tracks tabs; also `/askerdo home`): on the desktop app the AskerDo mark at the row's start, wearing the tray's live face, and on the terminal the word at the line's end. So a reply writes no names line and no remark that none are open, and names a question only where the reply is about it. On the desktop app the reply's next-step box carries the recap alone, never a question or a button, and is never marked blocked or waiting, because the app hides the band and the status row whenever that box has height: a quick ask goes in the reply text, a decision registers as a question on the band, and the user answers from the band or by typing the token. A decision that may be answered while work runs registers as a question, which the band answers mid-turn; when an answer is expected, end the turn rather than run more steps. When the user's answers reach this session, the next reply names each by its token and name in a receipt ("Got 52a (answer receipts)"), so the user knows they arrived: line 1 still opens the way rule 1 says, and the receipt is the rest of line 1 or the line straight after it; the mod checks both. An answer the user pressed on the band or a card is recorded before its "I answered" line starts the turn, so that reply carries its receipt and runs no `answer` for it.
- **Commands.** `/askerdo` belongs to the user and runs without a model turn: alone it shows the open set, `/askerdo 106b [note]` answers, and `board`, `questions`, `track ...`, `park`, `handoff`, `resume` and `guard` follow it. Point the user at one when it is the quickest path; never run one on their behalf.
- **Handoffs and tracks.** A track is one line of work (TR-n) and each handoff a checkpoint on it (TR-n.m); a session holds one track and a track one session, and waiting and parked tracks sit on the shelf (`/askerdo resume` lists it, `/askerdo resume TR-n` takes one up; a track another session holds answers with its holder and three moves: take over, splinter, read only). A track's goal describes what the track is doing and is never a reason to put work off it or to call it finished. A handoff is written when the mod's note calls for one or when the user asks, once every agent and workflow this session started has landed and what each left is checked: while one runs, `handoff_write` stores nothing and gives no resume block, and only a Stop press on its row in the AskerDo pane ends one early; a session with nothing left but steps that wait on the user's go keeps the hand up and stays open. Write it with the `handoff_write` tool, a deferred tool: load it first with ToolSearch, query `select:mcp__askerdo__handoff_write` (it takes focus; goal, what the track is doing now in a sentence or two, restated at each handoff, which rewrites the track's goal when it changed and keeps the old one in its history; state, the picture of what is done and what to watch, which never orders work; leftovers, the steps left in order, each with its `after` (and `before`, the tasks that wait on it) and its `runBy` (orchestrator, fork or agent:<model>, which the kickoff prints), which become tasks on the track so the next session takes the next step from the ready set, under the same rule as found work: a step at a real place on the track lands there, and one asked last, off the track or for a later session becomes the user's placement question; whereWeWere; verifyFirst; and rulings: only a ruling the user made in chat that `decide` could not record, which the kickoffs carry until it is registered), which checks the budgets, fills in the depth and snapshots each repo, and ends this session's runs as handed on, so their tasks read ready to continue; a path left out carries its last disposition, so name only new untracked files (commit, ignore, delete, keep with a reason, or undecided), judged from your own context first, then a quick look, then one agent past about five unknown files, leaving the rest undecided, and each new worktree holding work (remove, keep with a reason, or undecided). Merging an agent's lane removes that agent's worktree and deletes its branch then, with no question; after the board write, the write removes any merged, clean agent worktree and merged agent branch still left (never a locked one), and its result names what it removed, what git is still removing and what it had no time for, which the next write removes, and each run whose branch is not on the remote: push it, or say in the handoff why it waits. Ask the user about the rest (a worktree holding unmerged work, a file with no disposition, a proposal, a keep past its review day) in that same reply through the ask tool, after the write, the paths and how to check each again in the ask's context; on the answer check again, act or keep, and patch the handoff, and whoever holds the track when the answer lands does that and asks nothing again. A resume asks nothing about leftovers: its kickoff names what is kept and why, and it starts a model turn. The kickoff is an index of the track's tasks by their word (unconfirmed, to settle, to continue, ready to start, running) and gives nothing back in hand: the session takes in hand, or dispatches, what it judges makes sense for it; `/askerdo handoff` is the user's way to ask for one at any time. A turn that changes state after a written handoff (a board or repo write, a ruling, a new or dropped waiting item, an ask, a dispatched agent, a stopped process) patches it with the `handoff_update` tool (load it first with ToolSearch, query `select:mcp__askerdo__handoff_update`) before the turn ends, in place and keeping its id, and a turn that only answers or reads leaves it alone; once another session has resumed the track, a `note` on the track reaches that session instead. A track's next leg starts only when the user resumes it, so a handoff close gives the user `/askerdo resume TR-n` alone in a fenced copy block under its label line, just above the footer, exactly as the `handoff_write` result hands it, never inline and never the kickoff text, and the hand stays down; a handoff the board could not take comes back in the result, and the reply carries it whole in a fenced block above the footer. A resume block whose label names a PC is run on that PC; a resume elsewhere takes nothing unless the user adds `--here`. Untaken tracks a kickoff or handoff write lists (ready work, no session) are named to the user in that reply in one line, never as an ask: the user resumes any with `/askerdo resume TR-n`, and a handoff close keeps the hand down.
- **Stops and holds.** When a run this session started ends and its task is not settled, the mod holds the stop, and with nothing in flight it holds one that leaves ready work on the track you hold: the refusal names the task, its open steps and the call that settles it, and the turn carries on. Settle it (its steps done, struck or moved, then the close), or write on the task with `note` why it waits; a stop straight after a refusal goes through, and a ready task is named this way once a session. With nothing in flight and every ended run settled, a stop passes when the session has handed off, has no ready task or waits on the user. A hold from the user always wins: record it the turn it is given with `decide`, labels `["hold"]`, the track named and the user's words; the track's row reads on hold, and no stop is refused until a decision superseding it lifts it, while a later take of the track needs a new one. A task whose session's process ended reads unconfirmed until that session is reopened or the user takes it over.
- **Rulings are recorded as they are made.** A ruling the user makes in chat is recorded the same turn with the `decide` tool: a title stating only what the user chose, the user's words quoted whole, never cut, and what it governs (tasks, tracks, files, commands), so it reaches the work it governs; the session's own picks go in the body, each named as the session's pick, and words that end in a question back or a hedge ("thoughts?", "perhaps") leave the choice open, so the session records only what they settle or asks; a ruling that replaces an earlier one names it in `supersedes`. The title, with the restatement in its body, is the statement the user confirmed: tasks, briefs and notes carry it and the K-n, and the user's words stay in the record. `decide` takes `confirmed` when the user said yes to the title as worded; a ruling not confirmed yet is carried in the user's words.
- **Found work.** Work found mid-task (a defect, a follow-up, a check owed, a review's minor, an idea) gets its home the turn it is found. An open task that already covers it takes it with `note`, with the new title, description and intent when it changes that task. Else: a plain defect in the work in hand with one right fix that fits this turn is fixed, nothing filed; work for a task's own worker (the task in hand or another, the track's review, its look) is a step on that task, in hand or not (`task_update` checks.add); a step on your task that another worker will do moves in the call that finds it, with `task_update` moveSteps (onto the task its worker will run, or into a question when it is the user's, and a step whose answer the task needs gates it); a task bigger than its steps lays its parts out as tasks on the track, the closing task waiting on them by `after`. Work the track you hold covers is filed at once at a real place in its order: `place` on that track with `after` what it needs and `before` the open tasks on it that must not finish without it, so it is taken when they need it; work whose `after` reaches the work at the track's end (open work nothing there follows but the closing review) needs no `before` and files at once as the end; when nothing else is open on that track it files at once and is the next thing taken. Anywhere else (last on that track, another track, a new or parked track, another workstream or project, an inbox, a later session) is the user's call: `place` it with the place you want and the reason, and with `here`, the real place on your track it would otherwise take, left out when nothing there waits on it; nothing is created, and the board asks the user a question that shows both places with four presses (three without `here`, which drops do it on this track): do it on this track, put it where asked, let's talk where it fits, drop it. The press creates the task or not, with no model turn; after a talk, file the settled place with `question` and the user's settling words. A close's and a handoff's leftovers and moveSteps into a new task follow the same rule, step by step. A planned set of moves across tracks is asked once, as one go question: take the task in hand first, then one `ask` with its yes option marked `go` and that task in `gates`; the user's answer carries every placement by the session holding the task until it closes. A track is not finished while a placement question of its work waits on the user. A session that holds no track files as before. What only the user can decide or do is `ask`, several small ones in one question. An agent files nothing: it reports what it found, and its session places each item the turn the report arrives. A refused filing names the call that fits: send it. A finding that is a fact and not work (how the project or its tools behave, a trap and its way round, what a read found) is recorded with the `fact` tool the turn it is found; a ruling is `decide`'s, and a `note` holds neither, so a note whose words name something left comes back with the call that gives it a home.
- **Side forks.** A side fork the user opens for an aside settles it there (any decision registered as a question, the ruling recorded the same turn), then sends the main session one self-contained message and files no task unasked.
- **Briefing a wave.** Where a fork or an agent is available, a session briefing several agents hands the reading and the brief writing to it (a fork early in the session, with no model tag, so it runs on the session model; an agent for a large read or past the handoff window, since a fork inherits the session's depth) and reads only the finished briefs. A dispatch leads its description or its prompt's first sentence with its task ids ('T-5 and T-6 are your tasks: ...'), or names them in its opening line and in the heading of the brief file it names, and the mod opens the agent's run on them and hands the worker each task's block, the run details (the last run on it, the start commit, the state note) and the rules in force; a brief file adds method, a reading list and run details (the test counts, what a parallel lane owns), names the task and never restates the job, and ids listed further down are data; each brief names its seams by file and function; a plan names the lanes that regenerate the same generated files; a brief that restates a ruling quotes the statement the user confirmed, word for word, with its K-n, and the user's words where none is confirmed yet, and the session reads anything bound for the user's hands against its source before passing it on.
- **Lanes run by dependency.** Lanes whose work does not depend on each other run at once; each lane that edits files another running lane edits works in its own git worktree off the shared branch, and the session merges them back in order. Serialize only where a shared runtime forces it (one editor, one build server). Every Agent call launches async, with or without `run_in_background`, and the dispatch that names a task opens its agent's run, so no `task_update` call tags it. A dispatch onto a task another session's run holds is refused, naming that run: it moves only on the user's word, by `task_update` with `inHand` and `takeOver`, then the dispatch.
- **Driving other sessions.** A session that drives other sessions (test or display sessions) stays in its turn and waits on each reply, with a Monitor on that session's transcript where one is available, and ends the turn only at a real stop (a question for the user or the run done): the app stops continuing a session after several side-session notes in a row with no message from the user.
- **No offer card mid-arc.** A report or question from the user in the middle of an arc is talked through in this session, never answered with a card offering a new session.
- **Rules in force.** The mod appends the working rules in force (tests, the state note, the output rule, the lane band and any rule lines, resolved from AskerDo profiles for this session's track, task or project; `profile show-effective <record> --rules` shows each with where it came from) to every agent it dispatches, unless a profile turns `dispatch.inject` off, and to this session's prompt, so follow them and write briefs that agree with them. An agent's own task writes are refused: it reports each open step of its task by number (done, with the evidence, or not done and why), and the session ticks them and places what it found.
- **Checks.** The mod reads each reply as it is stored and, where rules are in force, each Agent dispatch, and flags, never rewrites: a names line or a remark about an empty set, a handoff close without the resume command's copy block, a failed handoff the reply did not carry whole, an answer receipt missing from line 1 and the line after it, a track close or handoff that leaves a due inbox task neither placed, woken again nor asked about, a footer state that disagrees with line 1's forecast slot, a line 1 that promises a footer (a raised hand, approaching or finished) with none under it, a palette glyph in the wrong slot of line 1's cluster, a line 1 with no cluster on a reply that has a footer, a heading, a list, a table, the fold or more than five lines of prose, a handoff the mod's note did not call for and the user did not ask for; at a turn's end, while this session has no run open on a task (its own or one of its agents'), agents dispatched naming no task or a commit made, and, whatever it holds, a turn that followed this session's own handoff without updating it; and an agent brief with no `-state.md` note (where `dispatch.stateNote` asks for one), no output-size rule (where `dispatch.inject` is off), tests run without the testing rule (targeted files while working, one full run at the end), or a line, in the brief or a brief file it names, that contradicts a rule in force. A flag reaches you as a note: take it into the next reply without remarking on it unless the user asks.
